plugin.keccak-constants.step.initial.rc: ι XORs a round constant RC[i] into lane (0, 0) in each of the {{rounds}} rounds. FIPS 202 does not list the constants; it derives them (§3.2.5): an LFSR with the polynomial x⁸ + x⁶ + x⁵ + x⁴ + 1 outputs bits rc(t) (Algorithm 5), and RC[i] takes rc(7i + j) as bit 2^j − 1 for j = 0 … 6 (Algorithm 6). The register R starts at 10000000; the LFSR region shows it as one byte with bit k = R[k], so the start is 01. The RC region shows each constant as a 64-bit integer, most significant byte first, as tables print it. In the state, lanes are little-endian, so ι changes the first state bytes.
plugin.keccak-constants.step.round: Round {{round}}: the LFSR outputs rc({{tFirst}}) … rc({{tLast}}) = {{bits}}. They become bits 0, 1, 3, 7, 15, 31 and 63, all other bits stay 0: RC[{{round}}] = {{word}}. The register is now R = {{register}} (R[0] first).
plugin.keccak-constants.step.rcMatch: All {{rounds}} derived round constants equal the published table. Each one has at most seven set bits, at fixed positions, taken from a simple LFSR: no hidden choice.
plugin.keccak-constants.step.rcMismatch: {{mismatches}} of {{rounds}} derived round constants differ from the published table.
plugin.keccak-constants.step.initial.rho: ρ rotates each lane by its own offset (FIPS 202 §3.2.2, Algorithm 2). The offsets come from a walk over the lanes: start at (x, y) = (1, 0); in step t = 0 … {{steps}} − 1 give that lane the offset (t + 1)(t + 2)/2 mod 64, then move to (y, (2x + 3y) mod 5). Two facts make this work: the move is the matrix [[0, 1], [2, 3]] mod 5, which visits all 24 lanes other than (0, 0) before it returns to (1, 0); and the triangular numbers 1, 3, 6, … 300 are 24 different values mod 64. The grid shows the lane x + 5y in row y, column x.
plugin.keccak-constants.step.offset: t = {{t}}: lane ({{x}}, {{y}}) gets ({{t1}} · {{t2}})/2 = {{triangular}}, mod 64 = {{offset}}. Next: (y, 2x + 3y mod 5) = ({{nextX}}, {{nextY}}).
plugin.keccak-constants.step.offsetLast: t = {{t}}: lane ({{x}}, {{y}}) gets ({{t1}} · {{t2}})/2 = {{triangular}}, mod 64 = {{offset}}. The next position would be ({{nextX}}, {{nextY}}), the start: the matrix [[0, 1], [2, 3]] has order 24 mod 5, so the walk has visited every lane except (0, 0) exactly once.
plugin.keccak-constants.step.rhoMatch: The walk visited {{positions}} different lanes and produced {{offsets}} different offsets mod 64. Lane (0, 0) is never visited and keeps offset 0 (Algorithm 2, step 1). All 25 offsets equal FIPS 202 Table 2.
plugin.keccak-constants.step.rhoMismatch: The walk visited {{positions}} different lanes and produced {{offsets}} different offsets, but {{mismatches}} of the 25 offsets differ from FIPS 202 Table 2.
